title: Customer Experience Management Platforms: A Practical Guide
summary: Learn how to evaluate customer experience platforms for service, feedback, commerce, social channels, governance, and creator operations.
body_markdown:
## The customer-experience stack for social commerce


### Before purchase: questions and product fit


Shoppers may ask about product details, availability, delivery, returns, and compatibility through storefront chat or social channels. The official[Shopify Inbox](https://apps.shopify.com/inbox) listing, for example, describes storefront chat connected to catalog, policies, orders, and customer context. A merchant should confirm which channels and order systems its service platform can actually access.


### After purchase: service and resolution


Customer service needs a stable case record, ownership, service-level rules, order context, approved answers, and resolution status. Messages from different channels should not create duplicate cases or expose one customer's information to another. Track first response, time to resolution, reopen rate, reason, escalation, and customer confirmation where appropriate.


### Feedback and reviews: learn without manipulating


Reviews and survey comments can reveal product, shipping, and service problems, but collection must remain trustworthy. The[FTC's review guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/soliciting-paying-online-reviews-guide-marketers) advises against soliciting only likely positive reviewers, conditioning incentives on positive reviews, or suppressing honest criticism. Review practices must also follow local law and platform rules.


### Creator operations: connected, but distinct


Creators can surface recurring audience objections, confusing product claims, sample problems, and content questions. Reacher's official[Creator CRM page](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/creator-crm) describes tracking creator status, products, tags, samples, GMV, conversations, and briefs for TikTok Shop affiliate teams. That is creator relationship management, not general customer support. Connect approved creator insights to the CX process, but keep identity, permissions, obligations, and metrics appropriate to each group.
